packages.com.almworks.jira.structure.api.pinger: Internal scheduling helper that calls registered callbacks periodically on one shared, low-priority daemon thread. Meant for the plugin's own components; it is exported as a service but is not a supported extension point.
packages.com.almworks.jira.structure.api.planning: Read and update access to planning tasks: issue-like items that exist only inside the plugin (item type `CoreItemTypes.PLANNING_TASK`) and carry a subset of the standard issue fields plus values of supported custom fields. Marked internal; the contract may change between versions.
packages.com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process: Tracking and reporting of long-running background operations (backup, restore, maintenance, import/export, resynchronisation, automation runs). Contains a persistent process registry with status, progress, cancel flag and display parameters for a progress page, and lightweight in-memory progress reporting interfaces.
packages.com.almworks.jira.structure.api.property: Small key/value property stores kept in the plugin's own database tables: one global store and one store scoped to individual structures. Values are strings; numeric and boolean helpers convert on the fly.
packages.com.almworks.jira.structure.api.pull: Versioning primitives for incremental (pull-based) data delivery. A data source has a current `DataVersion`; a client that knows an older version asks for an update and receives either the changes since that version or a full replacement when the versions are not comparable.
packages.com.almworks.jira.structure.api.query: The structure query language: a query evaluated against a `Forest` that selects rows by their position in the hierarchy, by the issues they show (issue keys, issue IDs, embedded JQL) and by pluggable named constraints. Queries are obtained by parsing text (`StructureQueryParser`) or with a fluent builder (`StructureQueryBuilder`). Other plugins can add named constraints through the `structure-query-constraint` module type by implementing `StructureQueryConstraint`. The text syntax is described on `StructureQueryParser.parse(String)`.
packages.com.almworks.jira.structure.api.rest: Plain data-transfer objects used as JSON request and response bodies of the plugin's REST resources. They have public mutable fields, no validation, and static converters to and from the corresponding model types.
packages.com.almworks.jira.structure.api.rest.eff: JSON transfer objects that report the side effects ("effects") produced by automation in response to a forest change, grouped into batches that can be inspected and possibly undone.
packages.com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row: Rows, the building blocks of forests. A row is an immutable triple of a row ID (unique across the instance), an item identity and a semantics code; the same item can appear in many rows. The package holds the row manager service, the `StructureRow` contract with its standard implementations, and static helpers for special row IDs (super-root, temporary rows).
packages.com.almworks.jira.structure.api.settings: Global and per-user configuration of the plugin: which projects it is enabled for, application-level permissions and who holds them, default structures, preferences for the panel shown on issue and project pages, and the attribute sensitivity settings that control which computed values may be shown when they depend on items a user cannot see.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.pinger.P.summary: Service that repeatedly calls registered `Pinger.Pingable` callbacks at a requested period. Implemented by the plugin and available as an OSGi component; internal. All callbacks run on a single daemon thread of below-normal priority, which wakes up roughly every 166 ms, so periods are honoured only approximately and a slow callback delays all others. The thread is started on demand and exits after about two minutes with nothing registered. After the plugin stops, registrations are dropped and new ones are ignored.

members.MIN_PING_TIME: Smallest allowed ping period, 500 (milliseconds). `ping` rejects shorter periods.
members.ping(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.pin: Registers the callback (arg 1) to be called about every `period` milliseconds (arg 2). The first call happens roughly one period after registration. Returns immediately. Throws `NullPointerException` if the callback is null and `IllegalArgumentException` if the period is below `MIN_PING_TIME`. Registering the same callback twice creates two independent registrations. Silently ignored when the service has been stopped.
Removes every registration of the given callback (compared by identity). A call that is already running is not interrupted. Unknown callbacks and calls after shutdown are ignored; errors are logged, never thrown.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.pinger.P.summary: Callback registered with `Pinger`. Implemented by the caller. It is invoked on the pinger's shared background thread, never concurrently with itself for one registration.

members.ping(long): Called once per period. The argument is the current value of `System.nanoTime()` at the start of the ping round (useful only for measuring elapsed time). Return `true` to keep being called, `false` to be unregistered. Throwing any exception (or linkage error) also unregisters the callback; the error is logged as a warning.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process..summary: The side of a background process that the worker uses: report status and poll for cancellation. Obtained from `ProcessHandleManager.getFeedback(Long)` or as part of a `ProcessHandle`.

members.setStatus(com.almworks.jira.structure.ap: Stores a new status for the process and refreshes its timestamp (the timestamp drives automatic cleanup, see `ProcessHandleManager`). A null status is ignored. If the process record no longer exists the call does nothing (an error is logged).
members.isCancelled(): True if someone has requested cancellation of the process (see `ProcessInfo.cancel()`). False if not, or if the process record no longer exists. The worker is expected to poll this and stop; nothing is interrupted automatically.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process..summary: Full handle to one background process, combining read access (`ProcessInfo`), worker feedback (`ProcessFeedback`) and display control (`ProcessUIController`). Returned by `ProcessHandleManager.createNew`. Handles are cheap views over the persistent process record: every call reads or writes the stored state (through a cache), so several handles for the same ID see the same data and the handle may be used from any thread or cluster node.

members.getId(): The process ID, a positive number assigned when the record was created. Use it to find the process again through `ProcessHandleManager`.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process..summary: Registry of background processes, kept in the plugin's database so that progress is visible across requests and cluster nodes. Implemented by the plugin and exported as a public OSGi component. No permission checks are made by this service; callers decide who may see a process with `ProcessInfo.isVisibleTo`. Process records whose timestamp (creation or last status change) is older than 30 days are deleted by the plugin's periodic maintenance, except those still referenced by automation.

members.createNew(com.atlassian.jira.user.Applic: Creates and stores a new process record with status `PENDING`, no activity, percent complete -1 (unknown) and not cancelled, and returns a handle to it. Arg 1 is the managing user (the only user who may see it; null means visible to everyone). Arg 2 is the display parameters, may be null. Throws `StructureRuntimeException` if the parameters cannot be serialized.
members.getInfo(Long): Returns a read view of the process with the given ID, or null if the ID is null or no such process exists (also null, with an error logged, if the record cannot be loaded).
members.getFeedback(Long): Returns the worker-side view of the process with the given ID, or null under the same conditions as `getInfo`.
members.getUIController(Long): Returns the display-control view of the process with the given ID, or null under the same conditions as `getInfo`.
members.delete(long): Deletes the process record with the given ID. Existing handles then behave as for a missing process (status null, percent -1, not cancelled; updates are ignored). Not determined: behaviour for an ID that does not exist (passed to the database layer as is).

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process..summary: Read view of a background process, plus the ability to request cancellation. Obtained from `ProcessHandleManager.getInfo(Long)` or a `ProcessHandle`. Values are read from the stored record at call time.

members.getStatus(): The current status, or null if the process record no longer exists.
members.getParameters(): The display parameters (name and buttons) last stored, or null if none were set or the record no longer exists.
members.isVisibleTo(com.atlassian.jira.user.Appl: True if the given user may see this process: when the process has no managing user, or the managing user equals the argument. A null argument matches only processes without a managing user. False if the record no longer exists.
members.getActivity(): Localizable description of what the process is doing right now, or null if never set or the record is gone.
members.getPercentComplete(): Progress in percent, 0 to 100, or -1 when unknown (not set yet, or the record is gone).
members.cancel(): Requests cancellation by setting the stored cancel flag (once set it cannot be cleared). Does nothing if already cancelled. It only signals the worker, which must poll `ProcessFeedback.isCancelled()`. If the record is gone the call is ignored.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process..summary: Life-cycle state of a background process. Each constant has a stable integer code used for storage.

members.PENDING: Created but not started yet. Code 0. Initial status of new processes.
members.FINISHED: Work has ended (successfully or not). Code 2.
members.getValue(): The integer storage code: 0, 1 or 2 as listed on the constants.
members.valueOf(int): Maps a storage code back to a status: 0 gives `PENDING`, 1 gives `RUNNING`, and any other number (including negatives) gives `FINISHED`. Never throws, never returns null.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process..summary: The side of a background process that controls what the progress page shows. Obtained from `ProcessHandleManager.getUIController(Long)` or a `ProcessHandle`.

members.setParameters(com.almworks.jira.structur: Replaces the stored display parameters. Null, or parameters equal to the stored ones, are ignored. If the record is gone, nothing happens (an error is logged).
Updates the current activity text (arg 1) and/or percent complete (arg 2). A null argument leaves that value unchanged; a value equal to the stored one is not rewritten. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if the percentage is outside -1..100 (-1 means unknown).

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process..summary: Read side of an in-memory progress tracker: lets an observer see what a task is doing, how far it is, and ask it to stop. The plugin's own tracker implements both this and `ProgressSink`; it is thread-safe.

members.getActivity(): The localizable description of the current activity, or null if none was set.
members.getPercentComplete(): Progress in percent, 0 to 100, rounded, including the scaled progress of delegated sub-sinks; -1 if the tracker has not been initialized with a positive total.
members.cancel(): Sets the cancelled flag. The worker sees it through `ProgressSink.isCancelled()`. Cancelling a delegate cancels the whole tracker.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process..summary: Write side of an in-memory progress tracker, used by code doing the work. Work is measured in abstract units: call `initialize` once with the total, then report units done. A part of the units can be handed to a sub-task with `delegate`, which gets its own sink with its own unit scale. In the plugin's implementation all methods are thread-safe.

members.setActivity(String, Object[]): Sets the current activity as an i18n key (arg 1) with message arguments (arg 2). On a delegate this sets the activity of the root tracker.
members.initialize(int): Sets the total number of units to the argument and resets progress to 0. Throws `IllegalStateException` if already initialized with a positive total, and `IllegalArgumentException` if the total is negative. Initializing with 0 is allowed but leaves the tracker unusable for `increment`, `setDone` and `delegate` (they then fail as not initialized).
members.increment(int): Marks the given number of additional units as done. Throws `IllegalStateException` if not initialized, and `IllegalArgumentException` if the count is negative or larger than the units still left (units already delegated count as used).
members.setDone(int): Sets the absolute number of units done. Throws `IllegalStateException` if not initialized, and `IllegalArgumentException` if the value is lower than the current done count or higher than the total.
members.complete(): Marks all remaining units of this sink as done (nothing to do if no units are left, including an uninitialized sink) and then completes every delegate created from it, recursively. Does not throw.
members.isCancelled(): True if `cancel()` was called on the tracker (or on any of its delegates, which share the flag). Also returns true, and sets the flag, when the calling thread has been interrupted; the thread's interrupt status is cleared in that case.
members.delegate(int): Reserves the given number of this sink's units for a sub-task and returns a new sink for it. The sub-sink must be initialized with its own total; its progress is scaled into the reserved units when computing percent complete. Activity, cancellation and the lock are shared with the parent. Throws `IllegalStateException` if this sink is not initialized and `IllegalArgumentException` if the count is negative or exceeds the units left.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.property.summary: Global string key/value store persisted in the plugin's database, with a non-expiring in-memory cache of values. Implemented by the plugin and exported as a public OSGi component. Internal API: no permission checks are made. Writing an empty or null value deletes the key. Values are read as strings; boolean and long helpers parse them.

members.getString(String, String): Returns the stored value for the key (arg 1), or the default (arg 2) when there is none. Never null when the default is not null. If loading fails, the default is returned and a warning logged.
members.getBoolean(String, boolean): Returns true if the stored value is exactly `true` (case-sensitive), false for any other stored value, and the default (arg 2) when no value is stored.
members.getLong(String, long): Returns the stored value parsed as a decimal long, or the default (arg 2) when no value is stored or it cannot be parsed.
members.set(String, String): Stores the value (arg 2) under the key (arg 1); a null or empty value deletes the key. The key is trimmed before storing and must not be null or blank (`IllegalArgumentException`). The local cache entry is refreshed. members.parse(String):
Parses query text into a `StructureQuery`. The returned query remembers the original text (`getQueryString`). The text is not validated against the instance here (unknown issues, invalid JQL field names and constraint argument errors are found by `validate`). Throws `NullPointerException` for null and `StructureException` (the plugin's own error 6005 `INVALID_SJQL`, category `INVALID_INPUT`, carrying the position and a localized message with up to 40 characters of context and line/column) for a syntax error.

Syntax (keywords are case-insensitive; multi-word keywords may be written with underscores or in camelCase, e.g. `prev_sibling` or `prevSibling`; whitespace between tokens is free):
- `A or B` (also `||`, `|`), `A and B` (also `&&`, `&`), `not A` (also `!`). `not` binds tightest, then `and`, then `or`. Parentheses group: `( ... )`.
- Basic constraints: `empty` or `null` (matches nothing); `leaf`/`leaves` (rows without children); `root`/`roots` (top-level rows); a comma-separated list of issue keys and/or numeric issue IDs, e.g. `PROJ-1, proj-2, 10001` (an issue key is letters/digits, a hyphen and digits, accepted in any letter case; a key or ID must be followed by end of text, whitespace or punctuation); embedded JQL in square brackets, e.g. `[status = Open ORDER BY key]` (the closing bracket is found while skipping single- and double-quoted strings, where backslash escapes the next character, and custom field references such as `cf[10010]`; an ORDER BY part is ignored; `[]` with an empty condition matches every issue row the user can see); or a named constraint (see below).
- Relational constraints: `RELATION OPERATOR C`, where C is a single clause (possibly negated, possibly itself relational; use parentheses for `and`/`or`). Relations: `self`; `issue`/`issues`; `child`/`children`/`sub_issue`/`sub_issues`; `parent`/`parents`; `descendant(s)`; `ancestor(s)`; `preceding_sibling`/`prev_sibling`/`previous_sibling` (plural forms too); `following_sibling`/`next_sibling` (plural too); `sibling(s)`. Combined forms `issue_or_R`, `issues_or_R`, `R_or_issue(s)`, `self_or_R`, `R_or_self` exist for R = child, parent, descendant, ancestor and the sibling relations, and relations can also be joined explicitly: `self or child in C`.
- Operators: `in`, `=`, `is` select rows having at least one relative of the given kind that matches C (e.g. `child in C` = rows with a child matching C; `ancestor in C` = rows below a row matching C). `of` selects the relatives themselves (e.g. `child of C` = children of rows matching C; `descendant of C` = everything below rows matching C). `not in`, `!=`, `is not` are the complement of `in`. When C is `empty`: `R in empty` / `R is empty` = rows having no such relative (`child is empty` = leaves); `R of empty` = rows that are not such a relative of any row (`child of empty` = roots). `self` is identity; `issue` is identity restricted to issue rows.
- Named constraints: `name(arg1, arg2, ...)`, `name()`, `name arg` (one argument, up to whitespace) or bare `name` when followed by `and`, `or`, `)` or the end. Names come from installed `structure-query-constraint` modules and are matched case-insensitively; the plugin itself defines `folder`, `memo`, `item`, `rowId` and `planningtask`. An unquoted argument runs up to the next `,` or `)` and is trimmed. A quoted argument uses `"..."` or `'...'`; inside it `\"`, `\'` and `\\` stand for the escaped character and any other backslash is kept literally. An empty argument between commas is a syntax error.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.settings.summary: Preferences for the plugin's panel on issue and project pages.
